findings.title: A policy waiver of a two-rule scan's second rule, accepted at base, now crashes gbg scan docs and the makedocs hard-scan gate with exit 3
locations: src/Scan.jl:398-408 (apply_ledger: the new LedgerError throw for a non-canonical policy entry)
src/CLI/Main.jl:148-151 (only Config.ConfigError is mapped to exit 2; LedgerError reaches the crash arm)
ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:50 (check("scan docs --hard-only", ...) calls scan_docs, which now throws)
src/CLI/Doctor.jl:343-346 (CFG.EXEMPTIONS names the entry, for any target)
test/scans.jl:181-203 (the base test asserting the waiver disables the scan, replaced by @test_throws)
findings.before:
enforced = unique!(vcat(String(row["rule"]), rules_for_scan(id)))
    for rule in enforced, e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy")
findings.after: isempty(e) || throw(Ledger.LedgerError("$rule on $(e[1]["target"]) is a policy waiver of a rule $id enforces but " * ...
findings.why_it_matters: Probe on the same fixture copy, base vs head. Waiver RULE.CIT.DOI (scope policy, target *): base gives gbg scan docs exit 2, --hard-only exit 0, CFG.EXEMPTIONS PASS. Head gives exit 3 on both, printing 'gbg scan: crashed — ledger: RULE.CIT.DOI on * is a policy waiver…' plus a Julia stacktrace. RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING at target * behaves the same (base 2/0, head 3/3). A waiver with a FILE target (RULE.CIT.DOI on src/FixtureA.jl) also goes from 2/0 to 3/3, though the canonical-rule path never gave a non-* target any effect. A consumer carrying such an entry had it rendered as a granted deviation and working at base. After bumping, every `gbg scan docs` and every docs build through the makedocs wrapper dies on it. The exit contract reads 3 as a crash of the tool, and the diff's own Main.jl arm treats a bad consumer config as exit 2. Refusing the entry is the documented design; a backtrace and exit 3 is not.
findings.description: The window replaced 'a waiver on any rule the scan enforces disables it' (base behaviour and base test) with a LedgerError for any policy entry on a non-canonical rule. The refusal is deliberate, and the doctor now names such entries. But the error goes out through the generic crash arm: exit 3 with a stacktrace from `gbg scan docs`, `--hard-only` and the docs wrapper. It is not reported as the consumer's cannot-evaluate (2). The refusal is also wider than the silently-wide defect it answers: it fires for a file-scoped target, which under canonical-only resolution would never have disabled anything.
findings.evidence: HEAD run: 'RULE.CIT.DOI target=*: gbg scan docs exit 3 / --hard-only exit 3 / CFG.EXEMPTIONS FAIL'; stderr 'gbg scan: crashed — ledger: RULE.CIT.DOI on src/FixtureA.jl is a policy waiver of a rule SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK enforces but does not own … Stacktrace: [1] apply_ledger(...) @ GBGCodingTools src/Scan.jl:405'. BASE run (3e30907 extract, same probe): 'RULE.CIT.DOI target=*: gbg scan docs exit 2 / --hard-only exit 0 / CFG.EXEMPTIONS PASS 1 entries'. Base test: '@test isempty(r.hits) && r.exempted > 0   # the waiver that was void'.

findings.why_it_matters: Ran prepare on a fixture check-consistency round with seed_salt and a built page carrying no anchor. HEAD: exit 0, 'WARNING — 8 seed class(es) … NOT planted', 'prepare: 0 seed(s) planted', and 'the payload directory now holds the SEEDED copies only' (nothing was seeded). BASE: exit 2, 'refused — 8 seed class(es) have no anchor in the manuscript'. The defect cited was a refusal that threw away a PARTIAL measurement. With zero classes planted there is nothing to keep, and check-docs still refuses exactly this ('a round that plants nothing measures nothing'). The two documentation instruments now disagree, and a consistency round whose recall is undefined for every class opens and banks.

findings.title: gbg round scripts --reason replaces the frozen scripts BEFORE refusing on a missing HEAD, so the refresh is never recorded
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:400-424 (refresh_scripts: install_script runs in the loop; the HEAD check and RoundError come after)
findings.before:
dst = Preflight.copy_scripts(cfg, String(rec["instrument"]), round)
    entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))
findings.after:
push!(moved, ...)
        Preflight.install_script(src, dst)
    end
    ...
    head = Git.head(cfg["root"])
    head === nothing && throw(RoundError("scripts: the root has no git HEAD to record the refresh against"))
findings.why_it_matters: Fixture round in a git repo with no commit. HEAD: `gbg round scripts <round> --reason "…"` exits 2 with 'the root has no git HEAD to record the refresh against', but lanes.js now exists in the round's workflow dir and scripts_refreshed is absent. After a commit the same call exits 0 with 'every frozen script … already equals the running copy's — nothing refreshed, nothing recorded', and scripts_refreshed is still absent. So the frozen scripts moved and no record will ever say so. That is the untraced refresh this verb and RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND ('recorded in ROUND.toml') exist to prevent. BASE: the same call exits 0, and the refresh is recorded (placeholder head).
findings.description: The rewrite dropped the placeholder head (a reasonable change), but it checks HEAD after replacing the files instead of before. A refusal that has already done the work, combined with the new 'no-op when nothing differs' rule, leaves the replacement permanently unrecorded.
findings.evidence: HEAD run: 'lanes.js before: false / round: scripts: the root has no git HEAD to record the refresh against / exit 2 / lanes.js after: true  scripts_refreshed recorded: false / scripts: every frozen script of 2026-01-01-check-docs-01 already equals the running copy's — nothing refreshed, nothing recorded / after a commit, the same call: exit 0  scripts_refreshed recorded: false'. BASE run: 'scripts: re-copied into … — refresh 1 of this round, recorded / exit 0 / scripts_refreshed recorded: true'.

findings.title: The claim-checklist narrowing drops claims of the very kinds it targets: backticked exit codes and subject—predicate clauses split at a spaced dash
locations: src/CLI/Preflight.jl:344-352 (CLAIM_EXIT third alternative now needs `[0-3]\s+[a-z]`; CLAIM_QUANTIFIER drops all/any/only; CLAIM_TOOL_ID needs a backtick before gbg; CLAIM_CLAUSE splits on ' — ')
test/rounds.jl:245-255 (the new tests pin only the intended exclusions)
findings.before:
const CLAIM_EXIT = r"…|\bexit\s+contract\b[^.]{0,60}?[0-3]\b"i
qu = occursin(CLAIM_QUANTIFIER, s) && occursin(CLAIM_TOOL_ID, s)
findings.after:
const CLAIM_EXIT = r"…|\bexit\s+contract\b[^.]{0,60}?(?<![\w.])[0-3]\s+[a-z]"i
const CLAIM_CLAUSE = r"(?<=[.;!?])\s+|\s+—\s+"
qu = any(c -> occursin(CLAIM_QUANTIFIER, c) && occursin(CLAIM_TOOL_ID, c), split(s, CLAIM_CLAUSE))
findings.why_it_matters: Re-ran the check-docs lanes' checklists on the head tree with the base regexes and the head regexes. 136 lines leave the checklists: 77 through dropping all/any/only, 49 through the clause split, 9 through the backtick requirement, 1 through the exit narrowing. That one is docs/src/guide/verbs.md:7, 'The exit contract is one for all: `0`' — the verbs page's statement of the contract, in exactly the house phrasing the third alternative was added to catch. The page backticks the codes, so `[0-3]\s+[a-z]` refuses it: 'The exit contract is one for all: `0` clean, `1` a finding' → false at head. The spaced-dash split cuts predicates from their subjects: ARCHITECTURE.md:1840 '`CFG.EXEMPTIONS` — and never ignores it' and ARCHITECTURE.md:1905 '`ROUND.OPEN` | lists open rounds (WARN; never FAIL' both leave the checklist. So do 2 unbackticked universal+verb lines in the same clause (Gate.jl:33, Passes.jl:479). The defects cited were the `1` of a version string and 'any verb anywhere on the line'; the fix is wider. The commit's per-lane totals reproduce (quantifier 245→110), but it does not say which claims went.
findings.description: The fix was aimed at version-string digits and line-wide conjunction. The narrowing also removes the backticked exit-contract phrasing used on the guide page, and it treats ' — ' as a clause boundary even where the house style uses it parenthetically between subject and predicate. The tests added pin only the intended exclusions, none of these losses.
findings.evidence: Classification of lines dropped at head: 'exit-narrowed (1) docs/src/guide/verbs.md:7 | … The exit contract is one for all: `0`'; 'strong+id-different-clause (49) … docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1840 | `CFG.EXEMPTIONS` — and never ignores it …; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1905 | | `ROUND.OPEN` | lists open rounds (WARN; never FAIL — …'; 'strong+unbackticked-gbg-same-clause (2) src/CLI/Gate.jl:33 …; src/CLI/Passes.jl:479 …'; 'weak-quantifier-only(all/any/only) (77)'. Regex probe: "The exit contract is one for all: `0` clean, `1` a finding" → false.
